review_notes: I read the complete 41-line target file and inspected the declarations it relies on: HomSpace.comp / HomSpace.comp_ofFragment (Skein/HomCompose.lean), HomSpace and HomSpace.ofFragment (Skein/HomSpaces.lean), HomSpace.ofFragment_congr (Skein/SkeinCategory.lean), bundleMap, composeBundleMap, bundleMapCompose and bundleMapClass (Skein/BundleMapClasses.lean), and the parallel class-level statement comp_bundleMapClass (Coordinates/StarClassFactor.lean), plus the use site in Coordinates/CapPeel.lean. The statement is over ℂ with an EdgeRankParameter, as is forced by HomSpace.comp, so there is no scalar-class generalisation available; n, m, u and the fragment X are already arbitrary. The one generalisation I found is in the shape of the composition: the fixed left factor bundleMapClass f e and the fixed right factor ofFragment X are both 'ofFragment' classes, so the result is an instance of a generic class-level composition lemma. I did not compile the proposed statement; its proof is the same rewriting already used in the target.

findings.problem: The statement fixes both factors to be classes of single fragments: the left factor is `bundleMapClass f e`, which is definitionally `HomSpace.ofFragment f.val (bundleMap e)` (BundleMapClasses.lean, `bundleMapClass`), and the right factor is `HomSpace.ofFragment f.val X`. It therefore only exposes one special case of the class-level rule 'composition of two fragment classes is the class of the composition, identified by a fragment equivalence', even though its proof (lines 38-39) uses exactly that generic rule (`HomSpace.comp_ofFragment` followed by `HomSpace.ofFragment_congr`). The same generic rule is re-derived independently by `comp_bundleMapClass` in Coordinates/StarClassFactor.lean (lines 41-50) and again in CapPeel.lean (line 455) and StarClassFactor.lean (lines 86-88), each unfolding `bundleMapClass` and then applying `ofFragment_congr`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the generic lemma in the composition layer (e.g. next to `HomSpace.comp_ofFragment`), and derive the current theorem from it:

  theorem HomSpace.comp_ofFragment_ofEquiv {s t u : ℕ}
      (F : Fragment (Fin (s + t))) (G : Fragment (Fin (t + u)))
      {H : Fragment (Fin (s + u))} (h : (F.compose G).Equiv H) :
      HomSpace.comp f s t u (HomSpace.ofFragment f.val F)
          (HomSpace.ofFragment f.val G) =
        HomSpace.ofFragment f.val H := by
    rw [HomSpace.comp_ofFragment]
    exact HomSpace.ofFragment_congr f h

Then `bundleMapClass_comp_left` becomes the instance with `F := bundleMap e`, `G := X`, `H := X.relabel (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans ((Equiv.sumCongr e.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin u))).trans finSumFinEquiv))`, `h := bundleMapCompose e X` (after unfolding `bundleMapClass`), and `comp_bundleMapClass` becomes the corresponding instance using `composeBundleMap e X` with the factors swapped. Proof works because `HomSpace.comp_ofFragment` (HomCompose.lean:97-108) rewrites the composition of two `ofFragment` classes to the class of `F.compose G`, and `HomSpace.ofFragment_congr` (SkeinCategory.lean:50-55) transports along any fragment equivalence. Degenerate cases are covered: s = t = u = 0 and the equivariant `Equiv.refl` instance of `Fragment.Equiv` are handled with no extra hypotheses, and the generic lemma keeps the exact same transport equivalence in the `bundleMapClass_comp_left` corollary, so no statement currently proved is lost.
findings.benefit: One lemma documents the standard pattern 'compose fragment classes, then identify the composite up to fragment equivalence', so users of the skein category do not have to reopen both `HomSpace.comp_ofFragment` and `HomSpace.ofFragment_congr`; the incoming-transport theorem here and the outgoing-transport theorem in StarClassFactor (and the call sites in CapPeel) become immediate corollaries of a single reusable interface, removing duplicated unfolding of `bundleMapClass` and duplicated two-step proofs.

theorem HomSpace.comp_ofFragment (s t u : ℕ)
    (F : Fragment (Fin (s + t))) (G : Fragment (Fin (t + u))) :
    HomSpace.comp f s t u (HomSpace.ofFragment f.val F)
        (HomSpace.ofFragment f.val G) =
      HomSpace.ofFragment f.val (F.compose G)

theorem HomSpace.ofFragment_congr {t : ℕ}
    {F G : Fragment (Fin t)} (h : F.Equiv G) :
    HomSpace.ofFragment f.val F =
      HomSpace.ofFragment f.val G
